title: In the whiteness
next_chapter_hook: When Chen Ji opened his eyes, a warm jade slip lay quietly in his palm, inscribed with an ancient character 'Pavilion' on the front, and on the back were seven chilling words—'Chapter Seven Hundred, Tianji Pavilion Awaits.'

text.content: The lingering impression of those eyes was branded into the depths of Chen Ji's soul. He sat cross-legged in the quiet chamber, and the surrounding spiritual energy of heaven and earth seemed to be drained by some invisible force, turning into a dead silence vacuum. Cold sweat slid slowly down his spine, soaking the meditation cushion beneath him. In that instant, he had clearly felt a gaze that transcended comprehension—it was not the spiritual sense of any powerful cultivator, nor the probing of sect elders, but something far more ancient and colder. 'Chess piece, you have finally been seen.' These words echoed repeatedly in his mind, each repetition striking his heart like a heavy hammer. Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the Tianji Record Fragment in his palm, his fingertips trembling slightly. He knew that from this moment on, he could no longer pretend to be just an ordinary废物 servant disciple.

Outside the quiet chamber, the night wind whimpered, making the window lattices creak. Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. He slowly unfolded the Tianji Record, revealing the fourth page, yellowed yet faintly shimmering with mysterious light. He had never used this page before, because each page's deduction consumed precious Heavenly Fate Value—each use cost five points. 'Five points of Heavenly Fate...' he murmured to himself, a self-deprecating arc forming at the corner of his lips. For others, this might merely be a number in their cultivation progress; but for him, every point of Heavenly Fate meant the erosion of his lifespan, meant the approach of death. Yet at this moment, he had no retreat. Since the owner of those eyes had already seen him, they would not let go easily. Better to take the initiative than wait for death—using the Tianji Record to deduce the other's true capabilities.

dialogue.content: The ink on the fragment suddenly glowed faintly, and an old and ethereal voice sounded beside Chen Ji's ear: 'Boy, you're mad.' Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul trembled slightly, carrying a rare solemnity. 'The fourth page of the Tianji Record corresponds to the deduction of the 'River of Fate', and its backlash far exceeds what you can withstand. If you forcibly use it, you may not complete the deduction but instead have your soul devoured by the River of Fate.' Chen Ji did not respond, merely injecting a wisp of spiritual sense into the fourth page. In an instant, intense pain exploded from his brow center, as if thousands of silver needles were simultaneously piercing into his mind. Mo Xiansheng sighed and fell silent, only quietly floating nearby, using his remnant soul's power to protect Chen Ji's last trace of mental clarity.

choice.prompt: The fourth page of the Tianji Record is activated, deduction is about to begin. Chen Ji needs to decide the target of deduction—with his limited Heavenly Fate Value, where should he direct it?

choices.text: Deduce the identity of those eyes
choices.description: Directly trace the source of the gazer, using the power of the Tianji Record to penetrate the layers of mist and uncover the truth behind those eyes.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial intelligence, but may expose one's position
choices.risk_hint: Since the other party can see you, it means their level far exceeds the deduction range of the Tianji Record, and one may suffer backlash

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth, pouring all ten points of Heavenly Fate into the fourth page. In an instant, the Tianji Record blazed with blinding white light, and an invisible vortex surged from the fragment,裹挟着他的神识冲向未知的深处。墨先生惊呼出声，想要阻止却已来不及。

choices.text: Deduce the origin of the Tianji Record
choices.description: Temporarily set aside the threat of those eyes, and instead trace the origin of the Tianji Record itself, perhaps finding the key to breaking the predicament.
choices.visible_reward: May obtain clues to the core secrets of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: Deducing things related to oneself results in less backlash, but the information may not be direct enough

text.content: Chen Ji's thoughts shifted, turning the deduction's target toward himself. He did not trace those eyes, but instead sank his spiritual sense into the core of the Tianji Record, tracing the origin of this mysterious fragment. The white light initially appearing was much gentler than before, yet also concealed hidden dangers.

choices.text: Defensive offense, setting up a smokescreen
choices.description: Without using the power of the Tianji Record, instead using Ye Qing's Demonic Path mist to conceal one's own aura, making those eyes lose their target.
choices.visible_cost: Need to contact Ye Qing for assistance
choices.visible_reward: Temporarily escape the gaze, buying buffer time
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing may not arrive in time, and the mist can only delay but not cure the problem

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly stopped his movements, his fingers gently stroking the edge of the Tianji Record. He thought of Ye Qing's Demonic Path mist—that was an excellent means of concealing Heavenly Secrets aura. Rather than recklessly deducing and alerting the enemy, better to first make the other party lose track of him. However, the moment this thought arose, the wooden door of the quiet chamber was gently knocked.

The deduction process was far from what Chen Ji had anticipated. The moment his spiritual sense touched the fourth page, the entire quiet chamber seemed to fall into a chaotic void. No light, no sound, only boundless white wrapping around him. That white was not ordinary whiteness, but a suffocating, pure, pale color that seemed to devour all existence. Chen Ji felt like a small boat, floating on the vast ocean of fate, surrounded by the same color in all directions, unable to distinguish up from down, nor past from future. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul anxiously shouted in the depths of his spiritual sense, yet seemed separated by a heavy barrier, unable to reach his ears. This white world was telling him—you have stepped into a realm you should not have entered, and everything from now on, you will have to bear alone.

"Just as Chen Ji was nearly swallowed by this whiteness, a blurred outline suddenly emerged in the distance. It was a massive chessboard, spanning across the Void, with countless black and white pieces scattered upon it. Chen Ji instinctively focused his gaze, only to discover that those pieces were not motionless—they were slowly moving, each move sending ripples that churned the entire chessboard into turbulent storms. What was even more chilling was that the shapes of those pieces were not the usual round or square forms, but... human shapes! Each humanoid piece corresponded to a blurred figure, some with indecipherable faces, others barely distinguishable—and in one instant, Chen Ji even glimpsed a familiar silhouette, that of Ling Yuan's aged and sinister visage!"

"Countless chessboards flashed before Chen Ji's eyes like a carousel, each displaying entirely different fates. Some depicted struggles between sects, others the rise and fall of dynasties, and still others the life and death, glory and humiliation of individuals. And above all these chessboards, there was always a pair of eyes watching—not the cold gaze from before, but an overlap of countless eyes, coming from different eras and different worlds, yet all possessing the same冷漠 and otherworldliness. Finally, at the edge of one particular chessboard, Chen Ji saw a row of faintly visible text—'Tianji Pavilion · Chess Observer · Chess Player · Chess Piece'. The calligraphy was ancient and vigorous, exuding a terrifying majesty, as if merely glancing at it would bring upon immense karma."

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji!" An urgent cry came from outside the door, Su Qingyao's clear yet slightly anxious voice. She pushed the door open and entered, just in time to see Chen Ji's body shudder violently, a trickle of blood flowing from his mouth, while his eyes stared straight into the Void, his pupils reflecting an unsettling whiteness. "What are you doing?!" Su Qingyao rushed forward in three swift steps, catching the staggering Chen Ji. The moment her palm touched his back, a cold breath surged into her arm—that was... the aura of the Tianji Record! Su Qingyao's pupils constricted, and she glanced at the yellowed fragment in Chen Ji's hand, a complex light flickering in her gaze.

choice.prompt: "Su Qingyao had already sensed the existence of the Tianji Record, and Chen Ji was at a critical moment of divination. How should he deal with this woman who was both a confidante and an investigator?"

choices.description: "Reveal some of the secrets of the Tianji Record to Su Qingyao, gain her understanding and trust, and obtain a reliable ally in times of crisis."
choices.visible_cost: "Expose one's trump card, weakening the advantage of playing the weak to devour the strong"
choices.visible_reward: "Su Qingyao's affection and trust increase significantly, possibly gaining her full assistance"
choices.risk_hint: "Although Su Qingyao is trustworthy, her stance is closely tied to the Tianqing Sect, and information leakage poses risks"

text.content: "Chen Ji felt the warmth from Su Qingyao's palm. After a moment of hesitation, he chose a compromising statement: 'I was attempting to divine a threat... it has already set its sights on me.' He did not mention the specific abilities of the Tianji Record, only vaguely stating the source of the danger. Su Qingyao fell silent for a moment, then suddenly pressed her other hand against his back as well, channeling pure spiritual energy into his body, helping stabilize his wavering soul."

choices.memory_label: 苏青瑶第一次见到天机录实物，震惊但选择守护

choices.description: "Clench teeth and reveal no information, using the weak body as an excuse to push back Su Qingyao's questions."
choices.visible_cost: "May damage the relationship with Su Qingyao"
choices.visible_reward: "Keep the secret of the Tianji Record and maintain the worthless persona"
choices.risk_hint: "Su Qingyao has already grown suspicious; continued concealment may backfire"

text.content: "Chen Ji forced out a bitter smile and said in a hoarse voice: 'Senior Sister Su, please don't worry, I just... had an accident during cultivation.' As he spoke, he casually concealed the Tianji Record into his sleeve, his movements fluid as if nothing had happened. Su Qingyao frowned, her gaze lingering on that sleeve containing the fragment for a moment, but she did not press further."

choices.description: "Tell Su Qingyao that someone is watching from the shadows, but conceal the existence of the Tianji Record, observe her reaction, and then decide the next step."
choices.visible_cost: "May arouse more suspicion from Su Qingyao"
choices.visible_reward: "Obtain information without exposing one's trump card"
choices.risk_hint: "Su Qingyao is extremely sharp; any flaw may be seized upon"

text.content: "Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze meeting Su Qingyao's. Those eyes that usually appeared murky were now revealing a terrifying sharpness. 'Someone is watching me,' he said softly, 'an existence more terrifying than Sect Master Ling.' Su Qingyao's pupils slightly dilated. As the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, she naturally knew what Ling Yuan represented—one of the figures standing at the pinnacle of this continent. An existence more terrifying than Ling Yuan? What level of being could that be? She did not speak, only silently strengthening the spiritual energy protecting Chen Ji, while her gaze grew deeper."

"Su Qingyao's spiritual energy flowed like a gentle stream, warm yet firm, pouring into Chen Ji's body. She did not ask more, only silently standing guard beside him, protecting him in her own way. The atmosphere in the quiet chamber became subtle—one was an Inner Disciple Senior Fellow who had long coveted the Tianji Record, the other a worthless servant-disciple holding the fragment yet forced to hide it. At this moment, however, they sat side by side due to a sudden crisis, and that invisible barrier between them seemed to be quietly loosening. Su Qingyao's gaze fell on Chen Ji's pale profile, and a complex emotion stirred in her heart. She recalled countless times when her probes had been easily deflected by him, those seemingly timid yet unfathomable eyes—too many secrets lay hidden in this person, yet she time and again chose to let go. This time... perhaps it was time for a different approach. 'If you're willing to talk, I'm always here.' Su Qingyao's voice was soft, so soft it nearly dissolved into the night, 'But if you don't want to speak, I won't force you.'"

"Chen Ji felt the warmth of that spiritual energy and his heart stirred slightly. Su Qingyao's trust was hard-won—she was, after all, the person most likely in the entire Tianqing Sect to see through his disguise. Yet at this moment, he truly had no mind to savor this unexpected warmth. Because in the depths of his consciousness, that white divination was still continuing. Countless chessboard shadows had already dissipated, replaced by a majestic palace. The palace gates were tightly shut, and above the lintel hung a plaque bearing three ancient characters—'Tianji Pavilion'. And beneath the plaque, a line of smaller text: 'Observe Chess to See the World, Play Chess Through the Ages, Pieces Through Reincarnation.' Chen Ji's heart lurched. Tianji Pavilion—he had finally seen the materialized form of that name. So the Tianji Record was not a product of the Heavenly Dao, but an artifact refined by an organization called the 'Tianji Pavilion'!"

"The scene of divination began to violently distort. The Tianji Pavilion's palace gradually collapsed, breaking into countless fragments that rushed toward Chen Ji. Each fragment carried an ocean of information—the names of Tianji Pavilion's历代 masters, the earth-shaking chess games they had orchestrated, countless fates and dynasties manipulated as chess pieces. Chen Ji felt as if he had been swept into a torrent of information. Had it not been for Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul desperately protecting his consciousness, he would have been washed away into oblivion. 'Enough!' Mo Xiansheng's voice exploded in his mind, 'Continue any further, and you'll be overwhelmed by this information!' Chen Ji gritted his teeth and forcibly interrupted the divination. In an instant, the white world shattered like a mirror, and his consciousness returned to reality. And the moment he opened his eyes, a cold object landed in his palm. Looking down, it was actually a warm jade slip, carved with an ancient 'Pavilion' character. On the back, seven chilling words—'Chapter Seven Hundred, Tianji Pavilion Awaits'."

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul trembled violently, and a rare note of horror crept into his voice: "Impossible... This is impossible... How could an unawakened writer have触及 the core secrets of the Tianji Record?" Chen Ji held the Jade Slip in his grasp, his knuckles white from exertion. He asked coldly: "What exactly is the Tianji Pavilion?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a long moment before speaking slowly: "It is an existence far more ancient than the Eye of Heavenly Dao... the true hand that moves the pieces behind the chessboard of fate across all worlds." His voice carried a tremor, "Boy, you've gotten yourself into serious trouble. The Tianji Pavilion never lets the pieces come to them willingly—unless you have already been selected as..." Before he could finish, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul suddenly fluctuated violently, as if touching some kind of prohibition, unable to continue.

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the Jade Slip into his sleeve, his expression terrifyingly calm. He had long grown accustomed to remaining composed in desperate situations—this was an instinct honed through countless moments at the threshold between life and death. The Tianji Pavilion, the Chess Players, the Eye of Heavenly Dao... these pieces of information rapidly connected in his mind, assembling a chilling truth: so it turned out the Eye of Heavenly Dao was not the final boss, and the Tianji Record was merely one of the pieces set in motion by the Tianji Pavilion. Those prophesied ones chosen by the Tianji Record throughout the ages were from the start merely pitiful puppets manipulated by the Tianji Pavilion. And he, Chen Ji, was no more than one of them. But so what? Since he had already glimpsed the outline of the chessboard, he would become the one who overturned it. "Tianji Pavilion..." he murmured the name, a cold smile curling at the corner of his lips, "Very well, I will remember you."

Su Qingyao watched Chen Ji recover swiftly from his earlier weakness, her heart secretly astonished. She noticed a change in Chen Ji's gaze—it was no longer the turbidity and timidity that belonged to a废物 servant, but rather a depth and coldness born of worldly experience. Such a look, she had only seen on one person before—the expression Ling Yuan, the former Sect Master, would display when orchestrating matters of the world. "You..." Su Qingyao started to speak, only to be interrupted by Chen Ji's raised hand. "Senior Sister Su, what happened today, please keep it strictly confidential." Chen Ji's tone was placid, yet carried an indisputable authority, "Not because I don't trust you, but because the more you know, the more dangerous it becomes for you." Su Qingyao stared at him blankly, suddenly realizing this servant disciple who was usually timid and submissive had somehow risen to a height beyond her reach. "Who exactly are you?" she murmured, her voice carrying a tremor she herself had not noticed.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's direct questioning struck at the core, and Chen Ji had to respond. Should he continue to hide his depths, or lift a corner of his mask?

choices.description: Reveal a vulnerable side, tell Su Qingyao that he is merely a pitiful person caught in the clutches of fate, longing for understanding and help.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing weakness may lower his image in Su Qingyao's heart
choices.visible_reward: Establish a deeper emotional connection with Su Qingyao
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao has seen too much pretense and may see through this as a performance

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then suddenly sighed softly. His straight spine curved slightly, as if shedding some kind of mask. "Who am I?" He shook his head with a bitter smile, "I am merely someone who doesn't want to die, yet must go to his death anyway." He raised his head, his gaze carrying weariness and helplessness, "Senior Sister Su, do you want to know the truth? But even if I told you, could you bear it?" Su Qingyao looked at this man who seemed to have aged ten years in an instant, and a soft corner of her heart was deeply touched. She opened her mouth, wanting to say something, but found her throat blocked by something.

choices.memory_label: 陈机第一次在苏青瑶面前展露脆弱，引发她的保护欲

choices.description: Speak with profit, tell Su Qingyao that following him promises endless benefits, exchanging her silence and support with practical gains.
choices.visible_cost: May make Su Qingyao feel used
choices.visible_reward: Gain substantive support from a powerful ally
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao is of noble character—too transactional an approach may backfire

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze suddenly turned sharp as a blade, his voice cooling: "Senior Sister Su, you are a wise person and should understand that some things are better left unknown." He paused, taking out an ordinary Elixir from his sleeve, "This is a Second-Grade Mind-Calming Elixir I acquired by chance. It has remarkable effects on stabilizing the soul. Consider it today's token of appreciation—thank you for your protection." Su Qingyao took the Elixir, her gaze complex as she studied Chen Ji. This man was full of secrets, yet he chose to dismiss everything with such a worldly approach. She couldn't tell if this was distance or protection. "You always do this," she said quietly, "pushing away everyone who gets close."

choices.description: Do not answer Su Qingyao's question directly, leaving only a meaningful remark for her to guess and ponder over.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the air of mystery, making her even more curious
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao's curiosity may drive her to investigate further

text.content: Chen Ji rose slowly and straightened his slightly disheveled clothes. His movements were unhurried, as if the heart-pounding deduction from before had been but an insignificant dream. "Who am I?" he softly repeated Su Qingyao's question, a meaningful curve forming at the corner of his lips, "Perhaps the answer to that question will come a long time from now." He turned toward the window and pushed open the wooden frame that creaked in the night wind, glancing back at Su Qingyao, "Senior Sister Su, the night is deep. If you truly wish to know the answer, then keep watching me—I will give you your chance." With that, he leaped into the night, his figure vanishing in an instant into the endless darkness.

Night wind poured into the quiet chamber, bringing a bone-piercing chill. Su Qingyao stood rooted in place, gazing toward where Chen Ji had disappeared, unable to recover for a long while. She looked down at the Mind-Calming Elixir in her hand, then recalled Chen Ji's complex, hard-to-decipher gaze from before, her heart stirred with rippling emotions. This man was like an unsolvable riddle—every time you thought you were drawing closer, you would discover a new barrier standing before you. But she was no one who gave up easily. Chen Ji said he would give her a chance, so she would wait—until the day he was willing to discard all masks. "Chen Ji..." Su Qingyao tucked the Elixir into her bosom, her voice low yet firm, "I, Su Qingyao, never go back on my word." Outside the window, moonlight fell like water upon the rooftops of the Tianqing Sect. In some unknown corner, Chen Ji held the Jade Slip in his hand, his gaze deep and profound as an abyss. "Chapter Seven Hundred... The Tianji Pavilion awaits." He murmured those seven words, a dangerous curve forming at the corner of his lips, "Since you wish to see me, I shall go and meet you." The Tianji Pavilion's chess game officially began from this moment.
